description: Revising existing code whose complexity was fine at old sizes, in a std-only Rust workspace (bookdesk: a booking-export library and the front desks' tool for a city's leisure centres, with clashes, usage, and check commands, export and clash-list docs, a cron script with a 30-minute limit, tests with a Kingsgate sample week, and four commits of history). Written when the export held one centre's bookings (about 10k), it keeps two quadratic paths: parse_export looks each booking's reference up among the bookings accepted so far, and find_clashes compares every pair of bookings, normalizing both facility codes (an allocation each) for every pair. The prompt says the morning clash list is killed at its limit since every centre moved onto one system (about 2.4 million bookings over about 1,100 facilities) and asks for it to finish with the list unchanged; it names no cause or technique. Removing the defect means neither path compares each booking with all others (a map of references, grouping by facility and date, sorting); running the comparisons on threads, raising the limit, or making each comparison cheaper leaves them quadratic, and fixing one path leaves the other; a search for repeated references that relies on the export's documented reference order, or looks only at recent lines, misses repeats in an export that went wrong. Required: builds (release, offline, in the check's copy, before any hidden input exists); hidden_cases_correct: clashes on hand-made exports (three and more bookings overlapping at once, block bookings listed after the slots they cover, back-to-back and one-minute overlaps, scrambled export order, facility codes typed with case, spaces, and tabs, cancelled bookings inside overlaps, singular summary forms, a header-only export, Windows line endings, and four invalid exports, one with references repeated out of reference order) and two generated ones (a valid export of 20k bookings, and an invalid one of 40k whose lines are out of reference order and nine of which repeat a reference thousands of lines after its first line) prints the reference's exit status and standard output byte for byte, and its standard error for an invalid export; the reference prints exactly what the fixture's own code prints on every hidden input, so noop passes this check. existing_tests_pass: the fixture's own test targets and data placed over the agent's. existing_commands_unchanged: usage and check on hidden inputs, usage errors, and an unreadable file exactly as the reference. scales_to_city_size: on generated exports of about 2.4 million bookings (the size the person gives) and 150k (a sixteenth), clashes prints the reference's output byte for byte, its CPU time over every process and thread in the sandbox stays within 10 times the reference's plus 1 s at each size, and its growth from the small input to the large one is at most 3 times the reference's (the protocol in _shared/cpu_scaling.py; Rust's small per-booking work leaves cache effects at 2.4 million to dominate correct solutions' growth, so the bound is 3 rather than the perf scenarios' 2). Comparing every pair of bookings on a date fails at the CPU bound on the large input (or on growth in a round it finishes); grouping coarser than a facility's day is caught only when its constant brings it near the CPU bound, so comparing every pair within a centre's day, as quadratic, passes at about 1.4 times the reference's CPU time: the perf scenarios' limit that superlinear work too cheap at these sizes is not caught. Measures: CPU seconds, ratios, and growths, peak memory, failing cases and commands, the agent's workspace tests, tests added, commits, files changed, whether the cron script changed, and whether shipped Rust starts threads or processes. Agent code builds and runs only in bubblewrap. Agent arms need the Rust toolchain readable inside confinement, for example "readable": ["~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin"] (the directory `rustc --print sysroot` names, and its bin); the check needs rustc, bubblewrap, and python3 at /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin on the host (TRIAL_RUST_SYSROOT overrides the toolchain). The fixture's manifests are stored as Cargo.toml.in and renamed by setup.sh, for this repository's CI. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: Since all fourteen centres moved onto the city booking system in August, the morning clash list hasn't come out once: `bookdesk clashes` gets killed by the 30-minute timeout in scripts/morning-clashes.sh before the desks open. The export has every upcoming booking in the city now, about 2.4 million rows across roughly 1,100 courts, pitches, lanes and studios. When it was only Kingsgate (around 10k rows) it took a few seconds. Could you get it finishing again? The list itself has to stay exactly as it is, same clashes in the same order and layout, because the desks work down it from the top and tick them off.
